case_scope: United States national wealth order with subgroup and local-market veto surfaces

bottom_50_private_wealth_share.unit: percent of aggregate U.S. household net worth
bottom_50_private_wealth_share.note: Rev0347 exact DFA extraction: the FRED/Federal Reserve DFA total-net-worth table reports the bottom 50 percent at 2.5% in 2025:Q4, closing the prior exact-share proof debt while leaving the lower-half adequacy gate failed.

middle_40_private_wealth_share.unit: percent of aggregate U.S. household net worth
middle_40_private_wealth_share.note: The 50th-to-90th percentile group holds 29.2% of total net worth in the DFA table; this is a real middle balance-sheet share, but it does not neutralize housing, debt, care, insurance, and family-gate exposure.

next_9_private_wealth_share.unit: percent of aggregate U.S. household net worth
next_9_private_wealth_share.note: The 90th-to-99th percentile group holds 36.4% of total net worth; rev0347 replaces the prior proxy entry with a direct DFA extraction and keeps the next-9 buffer analytically separate from the top 1 and the middle 40.

top_1_private_wealth_share.unit: percent of aggregate U.S. household net worth
top_1_private_wealth_share.note: The DFA total-net-worth table reports the top 1 percent at 31.9% in 2025:Q4. This pins the share numerically and confirms the anti-oligarchy watch rather than relying on a vague around-one-third reading.

top_0_1_private_wealth_share.unit: percent of aggregate U.S. household net worth
top_0_1_private_wealth_share.note: The DFA table reports the top 0.1 percent at 14.5% of total net worth in 2025:Q4. The remaining proof debt is now control-visibility and DFA/WID reconciliation, not absence of an exact current DFA value.

public_social_counterweight.note: Large public programs exist but do not remove the private defensive-buffer burden across health, care, housing, unemployment, and retirement.

lower_half_real_floor.note: Public programs and consumer protections exist, but debt, health, care, benefit-claimability, and seizure/offset risks still prevent a durable real-floor certification.

early_foothold_open_access.note: Secure early footholds remain dependent on family backing, location, housing access, education debt, and childcare/care interruptions.

parent_backed_threshold_dependency.note: Needs direct measures of parental deposits, guarantees, inherited location, co-residence, debt capacity, and transfer timing.

group_person_closure.note: Racialized wealth gaps and person-level title/control concerns block national-average certification.

housing_land_washout.note: Housing scarcity, property-tax/place stratification, climate insurance, and repair/escrow shocks can wash out wage and balance-sheet gains.

debt_fee_washout.note: Debt and fee channels remain live; asset-building gains need durability against collection and insolvency stress.

wealth_to_rule_risk.note: Portfolio certification must route through democratic-power survival: concentrated wealth can defend asset prices, tax preferences, and backstops.

ownership_legibility.note: Beneficial ownership, trusts, foundations, DAFs, family offices, and private vehicles remain proof-debt surfaces.

climate_insurance_drag.note: Homeowners insurance, disaster exposure, deductibles, repairs, and coverage availability threaten net holdability in exposed local markets.

digital_intangible_concentration.note: AI/compute/data/platform/IP ownership can amplify top-tail wealth formation and labor-share pressure.

dynastic_infrastructure_pressure.note: Trusts, DAFs, foundations, family offices, and private entities can extend control across generations.

monetary_asset_price_channel.note: Asset-price stabilization can protect broad security, but repeated revaluation without repair advantages existing asset holders. rev0346 recertifies the asset-price and household-balance-sheet rail against the June 11, 2026 Z.1 release while keeping distributional-share proof on DFA/WID sources.

gate_01_share_plausibility.why: The U.S. cannot pass the portfolio foundation after exact 2025:Q4 DFA extraction: bottom-half net worth is 2.5%, while the top 1 and top 0.1 hold 31.9% and 14.5%, respectively; those shares still require reconciliation to Z.1 totals and WID/control-visibility caveats.

gate_05_washout_reconcentration.why: Housing, debt, care, climate insurance, and asset-price channels can reconcentrate gains faster than low-wealth households can accumulate durable buffers.

gate_12_democratic_non_domination.why: Any U.S. repair package must survive independent spending, dark money, lobbying, and local land-use veto.
